# Appeal of Denial – Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**RE:** Rowan Carter, Member ID W914903090
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-19
**Reference number:** POC-5BA41AD17E-24277
**Payer/Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Missouri
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0660 - Knee Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html, last review 02/26/2026)

Dear Aetna Appeals Review Team,

I am appealing the denial of my request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which was denied on 2026-08-19 as "not medically necessary" (reference number POC-5BA41AD17E-24277). I am asking that Aetna reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I believe my medical records show that I meet the plan's own published criteria for this surgery.

## Why I believe this surgery meets Aetna's own criteria

**1. This is a single-compartment procedure, and my records show only one compartment is affected.**

Aetna's policy states that "unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is indicated when only 1 compartment is affected, and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is indicated when 2 or 3 compartments are affected." The policy also states that UKA "is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral)."

My MRI from 2026-06-09 shows full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes limited to the medial compartment. The procedure requested — a partial knee replacement — is a unicompartmental procedure, consistent with single-compartment disease.

**2. My imaging shows the type of severe, bone-on-bone disease the policy describes.**

The policy notes that "conservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint (medial and/or lateral but not patello-femoral) or severe angular deformity." My MRI documents bone-on-bone apposition in the medial, weight-bearing compartment.

**3. I completed a substantial course of non-surgical treatment before requesting surgery.**

The policy requires "History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management)" and states that members "should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record ... with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year."

My records show:
- Nine months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest.
- Fourteen weeks of supervised, in-person physical therapy (16 visits, 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-17), focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- Eight months of NSAID use with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-17, which gave only two weeks of partial relief.

This treatment history — nine months of symptoms, 14 weeks of formal in-person physical therapy, eight months of NSAIDs, and an injection — reflects the sustained, formal conservative care the policy describes.

**4. I do not have the absolute contraindications the policy lists — with one date I'd like the plan to confirm.**

The policy states that "Total joint replacement is considered not medically necessary in persons with any of the following absolute contraindications," including "Corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty." My injection was given on 2026-06-17. My records do not show an active infection or untreated substance use, and my BMI is 29. I am not aware that any other absolute contraindication applies to me. If the timing between my injection and the planned surgery date of [scheduled date of surgery] is part of the plan's concern, I would ask that this be clarified so it can be addressed directly.

The policy also states that "Members with relative contraindications should exhaust all nonsurgical treatment options." I am not aware that I have any relative contraindication noted in my records; my treatment history above reflects a full course of nonsurgical care.

## What I am asking for

Based on the criteria Aetna has published in CPB 0660, and the records from my physical therapy, imaging, and surgeon's office, I am asking Aetna to reverse this denial and approve the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) recommended by Dr. Marchetti.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the denial notice, and that the deadline stated on my denial letter controls; based on the notice I received, that date is 2027-02-15. I will submit this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, and will send it by fax to 859-425-3379 or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I am confirming before sending. I understand I can also call 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my member ID card with questions.

Please let me know if any additional records are needed from Dr. Marchetti's office or my physical therapist to complete this review.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

**Rowan Carter**
Member ID: W914903090
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date of signature]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
